findings.title: The pole predictor claims sectors whose QCD loop selection leaves out IR-divergent loops: gluon exchange between quark lines joined by a W/Z inside the loop (D19 u d > u d h, C07 u g > d t b~)
findings.checks: rule 4, every point, double-double and binary64, single pole of the leading sector only (D19 QCD^2 QED^6: 9.3e-2 .. 3.4e-1; C07 QCD^4 QED^4: 9.2e-4 .. 2.2e-2); the double poles agree
findings.evidence: rule 1 passes on both rows: our virtual equals MadLoop's per squared split order within 1e-12, poles included. Both follow MadLoop's [virt=QCD] loop selection (loops/orders.py LoopEligibility: every circulating species perturbative in a selected correction), so a loop carrying a W or Z next to the gluon (the boxes and pentagons exchanging a gluon between the two quark lines) is not computed. Catani's operator describes the complete O(alpha_s) virtual, whose non-factorisable poles <T_i.T_k> between the lines are nonzero when the Born interferes colour structures joined by different EW exchanges. Minimal reproducer on D19's points, double-double, rule 4 only (workspace/tmp/mq-validate/s2/ew22.py): u d > u d h QCD=0 (Z and W exchange, colour structures delta_13 delta_24 and delta_14 delta_23) single pole 1.6133954759575e-9 against the predicted 1.4436894729941e-9 (rel 0.105; 0.335 at point 1), while u c > u c h and u c~ > u c~ h (one colour structure, where the non-factorisable interference vanishes by colour) agree within 6e-33 .. 3e-31 and the QCD Born u d > u d within 9e-30. The operator's inputs are right: its Born vectors contracted with the Gram matrix give the engine's Born exactly (5.416202339758131e-9) and its C_ij are the expected colour algebra (s2/vec.py); the Python path (LoopSlice.evaluate, 34 digits) and the native executor give the same virtual and prediction (s2/catani-D19.log); no relabelling of the legs reproduces the virtual (24 tried, s2/perm-D19.log); the deviation is mu-independent (points 0 and 3: same kinematics, mu_R halved, the same -0.0313 x Born). poles.predicted_sectors only checks the trees left by a soft exchange of each coupling (L - 2c), not the loops the species condition removes. The same mechanism applies to C07 (W joining the light u->d line and the t b~ line). Pole selection (2026-10-28, workspace/tmp/mq-validate/s3/irmode-D19.log, D19 point 0, double-double, slice d3081568): poles='ir' returns the same virtual as poles='all' to every printed digit (finite -3.973456325044482e-9, single -1.613395475957548e-9, double -5.424950094330169e-10), its UV-origin pole parts are 0 and its IR-origin parts are the whole poles, so the renormalised virtual's IR poles are the computed ones (the user-facing 'ir' output is consistent with rule 1); only the Catani prediction (single -1.443689472994084e-9, double equal) misses.
findings.routed_to: coordinator: owner of loops/v2/poles.py predicted_sectors (a sector whose Born has colour-connected structures joined only by non-correction bosons with a nonzero non-factorisable <T_i.T_k> is not predicted, or the operator is restricted to the computed loops; poles='ir' itself is consistent, see the evidence). MQ-VALIDATE then moves the D19 and C07 sectors to unpredicted (rule 4 keeps checking them against MadLoop per split order)

findings.title: MadLoop's double-precision values: C01, C01@params, C02, D11 resolved by MQ-REF's fix round 2; A06 misses only against the G1 fixture's binary64 MadLoop, which MQ-REF's quadruple-precision rerun corrects
findings.checks: rule 1: A06 point 1 single pole 1.18e-12 against tests/fixtures/loop/required/uux_uux.json's MadLoop (status 216, own accuracy 0.0); resolved: C01 point 1 finite 3.25e-11, C01@params point 1 finite 2.69e-11, C02 point 0 finite 2.1e-12, D11 point 1 single pole 4.27e-12 (all pass at pt7)
findings.evidence: Cross-checks run into workspace/tmp/mq-validate/qpref/ (the committed exports read only; MQ-REF's toolkit, references.py run): (a) C01 point 1: MadLoop forced to quadruple precision (--madloop-accuracy 1e-20, status 328) reproduces its binary64 value (finite 5.527401070421307, 3.25e-11 from ours; single and double pole 4.8e-13 from ours, which equal Catani's within 1e-27), while Recola (COLLIER) agrees with our double-double within 1.1e-15 on every coefficient of points 0-3 (finite 5.527401070600913 at point 1); our double-double equals 40 and 60 digits within 1e-31 there (s2/c01ap.log): MadLoop's massive-b result is off, not ours. (b) C02 point 0 and D11 point 1: forced quadruple precision brings MadLoop within 5e-14 and 7e-15 of ours (Recola 5.7e-13, 1.5e-13): binary64 noise of the status-216 runs that MadLoop's estimate does not see. (c) A06 point 1 (a cancelling single pole, 0.12 against a Born of 302): the committed Recola and OpenLoops values are 7.3e-13 and 5.2e-13 from ours, MadLoop 1.18e-12; MLStabThres = 1e-20 cannot force quadruple precision there because MadLoop's binary64 estimate is exactly 0 (status 216 again). Not explained by the input point: double-double at MadLoop's own quadruple-precision point (its ImprovePSPoint=2 projection of the binary64 rounding, supplied_points.madloop_qp_point) gives the same deviations (workspace/tmp/mq-validate/qp/exp.py). MQ-REF's per-point records (fix round 06dfb9c5) show MadLoop's own inconsistency at the failing massive-b points: at C01 point 1 its printed Born and the Born its double pole implies differ by 4.82e-13 (C01@params point 1: 3.7e-13), against 3e-16 .. 1e-15 at the other rows' points; C02 point 0 and D11 point 1 show 3.3e-16 and 8.6e-16 (binary64 noise in the finite and single pole only). The fix round added no second provider to C01, C02, D11 (campaign pt6 at a765a9cc: the same five failures). Cause of the C01 miss (MQ-REF's fix-round-2 experiment, workspace/tmp/mq-ref/r3/c01_hf0 against c01_hf2, read only): MadLoop's numerical helicity filter (HelicityFilterLevel 2, the export's default) drops helicity configurations that vanish for a massless b but not for the massive one; with HelicityFilterLevel 0 MadLoop's C01 point 1 finite part is 5.527401070600928, 1.7e-15 from our double-double (5.5274010706009188), at its own binary64 accuracy 1.1e-15. MQ-REF's fix round 2 (in progress at 828ebaf0) reruns every point with the filter off and in quadruple precision. Campaign pt7 (2026-10-28, head f9fd78fd, MQ-REF fix round 2 75db7231: every point in MadLoop's quadruple-precision stage, HelicityFilterLevel 0, Recola as C01's second provider): C01, C01@params, C02 and D11 pass every rule (the default tier passes). A06 keeps its PLAN reference, the G1 three-provider fixture required/uux_uux.json (MadLoop binary64, status 216), where the miss stays; its MQ-REF quadruple-precision rerun at the same points plus mu_0/2 (variant A06@sectors, pt8) passes every rule with the point-1 single pole 2.8e-14 from double-double, and Recola and OpenLoops agree within 7.3e-13 and 5.2e-13.
findings.routed_to: coordinator: A06's primary reference (the G1 fixture's binary64 MadLoop) is superseded by MQ-REF's quadruple-precision rerun (A06@sectors, passing); proposal: make the rerun the primary of the rows whose PLAN reference is a G1 required fixture (A01, A06, A12, A13, A19, A20, A21, B01, B05, D07, D08, D09, D10, E06), keeping the G1 fixture's Recola and OpenLoops as the outlier route

findings.title: g g > u u~ u u~ and u u~ > g g g g g: no provider reaches 1e-12 at 2->4/2->5 (MadLoop quadruple precision 1.2e-11 with a 1e-12 IR-relation defect; Recola 5e-11; OpenLoops 2.6e-12)

findings.evidence: A18: MadLoop's quadruple-precision values (status 328/329, own accuracy 0) are up to 1.17e-11 (finite) and 1.06e-12 (double pole) from ours; MadLoop's double pole is off its own Born times the universal IR factor by exactly that 1.06e-12 at point 2 (and 3.5e-13 at points 0, 3), while ours equals Catani's within 9e-28 and our Born equals MadLoop's within 2e-15, so MadLoop's loop carries a ~1e-12 systematic error. Third opinions (workspace/tmp/mq-validate/qpref/): OpenLoops (ppjjjj, binary64) 5.5e-13 / 9.8e-13 / 1.2e-12 / 2.6e-12 on the finite part of points 0-3 and <= 1.8e-13 on the poles; Recola (binary64) up to 5.3e-11 with double poles 1.1e-11 off. The deviations do not move when our double-double is evaluated at MadLoop's quadruple-precision input point (qp/exp.py). A23 (MadLoop status 216, own accuracies 1.2e-13 .. 2.3e-12, covering some coefficients; Recola's double poles off the universal factor by up to 4.4e-11): no second provider within 1e-12; a forced quadruple-precision MadLoop 2->5 run was not attempted (estimated hours, HANDOFF §0.1). MQ-REF fix round 2 (75db7231): OpenLoops (ppjjjj) is A18's recorded second provider and MadLoop's points 0, 2, 3 are named OUTLIER in the fixture (CutTools quadruple precision, return code 329, own accuracy 0.0, its double pole off its Born x the universal factor by 3.5e-13 .. 1.1e-12). Campaign pt7: A18 misses at point 0 finite 3.45e-12 (OpenLoops 5.5e-13 from double-double), point 2 finite 6.37e-12 and double pole 1.06e-12 (OpenLoops 1.16e-12 and 1.1e-13), point 3 finite 1.17e-11 (OpenLoops 2.55e-12); rule 1 (i) cannot pass where MadLoop's own accuracy reads 0.0, and at points 2 and 3 no provider is within 1e-12 of double-double (whose poles equal Catani's within 1e-27). A23 (2->5, not regenerated) is unchanged.

findings.title: MadLoop's per-helicity references miss 1e-12 on suppressed helicities and on a cancelling finite part (A09@soft resolved)
findings.checks: A08 hel point 0: helicities h---+- and h+++-+ born 9.9e-11 (their Born 3.6e-11 against a summed Born of order 1) and their poles 1.3e-12 .. 8.1e-12, h-+-++ finite 4.5e-12 (a finite part 100x below its poles); A09@soft resolved
findings.evidence: A09@soft point 1: the loop coefficients agree within 2.5e-13 (the double pole = universal factor x MadLoop's internal Born), only the reported Born misses; our point equals MadLoop's quadruple-precision point within 4.9e-25, so the input does not explain it; a binary64 Born at a soft point carries the momentum-conservation rounding relative to the soft energy (1e-16 / 1e-5). A08: |ours - MadLoop| = 3.6e-21 for a helicity Born of 3.6e-11, i.e. 2 sqrt(B_h B_max) x 1e-16, the binary64 rounding of the amplitude of a helicity suppressed to 1e-11. The runner takes the per-sector Borns from born_matrix.f (binary64); MadLoop's own quadruple-precision evaluation (status 3xx) holds a quadruple-precision Born A09@soft: resolved by MQ-REF's fix round 06dfb9c5 (at madloop_qp_point points the reference Born is MadLoop's quadruple-precision double pole over the universal factor, born_source 'madloop_double_pole_over_universal_factor'): A09@soft passes every rule at pt6. A08 (status 328, quadruple precision) is unchanged: the per-helicity rows carry no born_source record, and at a rescued point MadLoop evaluates its own quadruple-precision repair of the binary64 point (~1e-16 from the published one), to which a helicity suppressed to 1e-11 and a finite part cancelling 100x are sensitive at the observed level. Resolved by MQ-REF's fix round 2 (75db7231) per-helicity reference records: at quadruple-precision entries the helicity Born is its double pole over the universal factor, and an entry whose printed binary64 Born misses that by more than 1e-13 (a helicity suppressed below the point's binary64 condition) or that vanishes is compared absolutely against the summed Born (72 of A08's 128 entries; the harness reads the record, rule_hel). A08 passes every rule at pt7; the formerly failing h---+-, h+++-+ (Born mismatch 1e-10) and h-+-++ (3.8e-13) are absolute entries now, h-+-++'s finite part within 8.4e-19 of a bound 3.5e-14 (strictly relative 4.5e-12 as before). The absolute per-helicity convention is MQ-REF's (pending its re-audit and the coordinator's acceptance); without it A08 fails as in pt6.

findings.evidence: C01 point 1 per virtual component, 40 against 60 digits (workspace/tmp/mq-validate/s2/apcomp.py): the bare loop's finite part 7.6e-33, its poles 1.2e-59; R2, UV, UV external fields, UV local and the Born 1e-59 .. 2e-59.
